title: Classes and Objects: Modelling Real Things
concepts: computing a value instead of storing it
class attribute shared by every object

ai_pair_moment.flaw: Asked to add free teas to Asha's LoyaltyCard (one free tea for every 10 stamps), the AI stored free_teas as an attribute and added one only when the stamps were exactly 10, and said a card with 25 stamps has 2 free teas. A real run showed 25 1, and Asha's cases showed that 25 stamps and an old card created with 12 stamps both failed. Computing free_teas() from the stamps (stamps // 10) made every case pass. Later the AI suggested a history list written in the class body; a test with two cards showed that Omar's card shared Lina's drinks, so Asha moved the list into __init__ and ran her pytest file again.

changes: The chapter uses the cafe's menu items, orders and a loyalty card, continuing Asha's Corner Cafe story from Chapter 25.
Inheritance is left out: the curriculum entry lists classes, objects, __init__, attributes, methods and data classes, and the chapter keeps to those.
The default print form of an object (a type name and a memory address) is shown only as an illustrative fragment, because the address changes on every run.

The AI section's classes live in small module files (card_ai.py, card_fixed.py, card_debug.py, card_lines.py, card_shared.py, card_final.py), so each test run imports one version of the class and the video can show the class and the run separately.
The lesson's data class ValueError traceback is shortened with '...' because it runs through the dataclasses module's own files; the full report is in the verified run.
outstanding_issues: On a learner's computer, the error reports show the full path to the file instead of the short file name.
The narration uses a synthetic voice (Kokoro bm_lewis). The owner should watch the video once and flag any word the voice mispronounces; fixes go in the PRONOUNCE list in tools/voice.py.
